newsitem.title: USA: Boston Partners launches first mutual fund.
newsitem.headline: Boston Partners launches first mutual fund.

text.p: Boston Partners Asset Management LP, the money management company formed by former executives of Mellon Bank Corp's Boston Co, launched its first mutual fund Tuesday.

Boston Partners Large Cap Value Fund is a diversified fund seeking long-term growth of capital, with current income as a secondary objective. It will primarily invest in common stocks and convertible securities of companies with a market capitalization of $1 billion or more, Boston Partners said.
The fund carries a minimum investment of $100,000 for institutional shares.

"Many investors have expressed interest in our products, which until now, have been exclusively geared towards large institutional investors," said Boston Partners Chairman Desmond Heathwood. "Now, smaller pension plans and individuals can invest with us as well."
However, the $10,000 minimum investment for individual shares may be prohibitive for many individual investors.
The fund will be managed by Mark Donovan and Wayne Sharp, senior vice presidents of Boston Partners' equity strategy commmittee.
Formed in April 1995, Boston Partners currently has more than $7 billion in assets under management for 70 clients, primarily institutional customers.
